text: Multiply any number at all by zero. What do you get?
Ben has 3 apples and buys a dozen more. How many apples does he have now?
How many legs do two spiders and two ants have between them?
why: Spiders have 8 legs and ants have 6: 16 + 12 = 28.

text: Skipping one letter each time: A, C, E, G. Which letter follows?
How many hours are there in three whole days?
At exactly three o'clock, what angle do a clock's two hands make?
why: A quarter of the way round the face: 360 ÷ 4 = 90.

text: Fill the gap in this run of numbers, each 4 apart: 3, 7, 11, __, 19
From midnight to midnight, how many minutes tick by?
Write RACECAR backwards. What word do you get?
why: It's a palindrome: it reads the same both ways.

text: The gaps shrink by one each time: a hundred, 90, 81, 73. Which number follows?
why: The gaps are 10, 9, 8, so the next is 7: 73 − 7 = 66.

text: Toss a coin three times in a row. How many different heads-and-tails sequences could you get?
Sally is 10 and her sister is half her age. When Sally is 70, how old will her sister be?
why: Her sister is 5 years younger, not half her age for ever: 70 − 5 = 65.

text: What is the first prime number after 20?
A train a mile long runs at a mile a minute into a tunnel a mile long. How many minutes from its front going in to its back coming out?
why: The front must travel the tunnel's mile plus the train's own mile.

text: A man has three daughters, and each daughter has one brother. How many children does he have?
why: The daughters all share the same brother: 3 girls + 1 boy.

text: Which is bigger: 2 multiplied by itself ten times, or 10 cubed?
Spelt out in English, which number has as many letters as its own value?
why: F-O-U-R has four letters; no other number word matches itself.

text: How many corners do a triangle and a hexagon have between them?
Rearrange the letters of STOP to spell things you cook in.
Spell out EXCELLENCE. Count its Es. What do you get?
